description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Common types used to implement standards in the other packages.
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- The packages no longer have a `net8.0` build. An application on .NET 8 or .NET 9 gets a .NET Standard build, without the APIs that only the `net10.0` build has, such as `DateOnly` and `TimeOnly` support. To keep those APIs, move the application to .NET 10.
- The `netstandard1.x` and `netstandard2.0` builds no longer list `JetBrains.Annotations` as a NuGet dependency. If your code uses its attributes and you got the package through DataStandardizer, add a reference to `JetBrains.Annotations` to your project.
- `StringEnum.TryParse(Type, …)` throws `ArgumentException` when `enumType` isn't a string enumeration, as `Enum.TryParse` does for a type that isn't an enum. It used to return `false`. A null `value` still returns `false`.
- StringEnum.GetNames and GetValues return members sorted by value (ordinal comparison), as System.Enum does, so Parse and TryParse with ignoreCase pick the first match in that order.
- StringEnum.GetValues returns one entry per member, including members that share a value, and GetValues(Type) returns an Array of the enumeration type instead of object[].
- StringEnum.Parse and TryParse with ignoreCase return the first member that matches ignoring case, in GetNames order, as System.Enum does, even when another member matches exactly.
- StringEnum.TryParse returns false for an empty value or one that is only white space, as System.Enum.TryParse does.
- StringEnum.Parse throws ArgumentException with the message "Requested value '…' was not found." and no parameter name for a value it doesn't find, as System.Enum.Parse does.

New:
- StringEnum.IsDefined(Type, object) and IsDefined<TEnum>(TEnum), which check a value of the enumeration, as System.Enum.IsDefined does.
- StringEnum.ToObject(Type, object), which takes a string or a value of any string enumeration, as System.Enum.ToObject(Type, object) does.
- StringEnum.Format(Type, object, string), which writes a value with the format strings of System.Enum.Format.
- StringEnum.Parse and TryParse overloads that take a ReadOnlySpan<char>, on .NET 10.

Fixed:
- Debuggers can step into the packages' source through Source Link.
- `StringEnum` no longer throws for a string enum whose nested class holds an instance field of the enum's type, such as the closure class of a lambda that captures one.
- `StringEnum` lists members declared in public nested classes at any depth, and no longer lists non-public static fields of nested classes.
- StringEnum.ToObject(Type, string) throws the conversion's own exception instead of TargetInvocationException.
- `StringEnum` no longer treats a struct as a string enumeration because it implements an unrelated interface named `IStringEnum`, and throws `ArgumentException` for an open generic definition instead of `InvalidOperationException`.
- `StringEnum` names the same parameter as `System.Enum` in `ArgumentNullException`: `TryParse(Type, …)` names `enumType` and `IsDefined<TEnum>` names `value`, and `Parse(Type, …)` and `ToObject(Type, string)` name `value` when both arguments are null.
- `TypeExtensions.GetMethod` throws `ArgumentNullException` for a null `obj` or `methodName`, and its documentation describes which methods the visibility flags match.
- StringEnum.Parse and TryParse ignore white space around a name or value, as System.Enum does.
- StringEnum.GetName(Type, object) accepts a string or a value of another string enumeration, as its documentation says and System.Enum.GetName does.

Deprecated and removed:
- `TypeExtensions.GetMethod` is obsolete and will be removed in a future major version.

Changed:
- The netstandard1.x and netstandard2.0 builds now carry nullable annotations, so projects on C# 8 or later with nullable enabled get null warnings from them.
- `StringEnum` throws an `InvalidOperationException`, from every member including `TryParse`, for a string enum in which two members share a name.
